name: underscores
label: Mom + Pop
lede: She started posting dubstep at 13, taught herself guitar to make a debut album, and wrote her best-reviewed record on escalators and in airports.

eras.title: Dubstep at thirteen
eras.text: A San Francisco kid with her dad's studio gear and a Skrillex obsession put out one-offs on SoundCloud for years, then started singing on her own records. The EPs are where the voice showed up.

years.p: [[underscores|ab1a3f85-e0ea-470a-af5c-175447ae774c]] starts uploading under a lowercase name, chasing the sound design she heard in Skrillex. In 2016 she finishes second in the Monstercat Mix Contest.
years.xp:
Wikipedia has her releasing dubstep and one-offs for years, among them the 2015 single "Mild Season", before she got bored of the sound-design loop and widened her palette. Her father, Ryan Downe, is an audio engineer, so the computers and instruments were already in the house.

The FADER quotes her acknowledging that: having gear around gave her an advantage, though not industry connections.

years.h: Skin Purifying Treatment, the first EP with words
years.p: The first project where she sings. According to Wikipedia, it largely works through questions about gender, and she has said being trans was all she could think about in high school.
years.xp: Two more EPs followed, We Never Got Strawberry Cake (2019, with a cover she designed herself and calls her proudest work) and Character Development! (2020). Jazz and future bass sit next to the songwriting.

eras.title: Guitar, gecs and a water tower
eras.text: Out of guitar tricks she barely knew, she made a debut that landed on year-end lists. Then came the road, and the fans who came for the gecs.

years.cap: Fishmonger (2021). Cover photographed in Longport, New Jersey.
years.h: Fishmonger: a hyperpop debut built on guitars she couldn't play
years.p: Recorded at her parents' house during the pandemic, self-released March 25, with a guitar on every song after she ran out of production tricks.
years.xp:
She told interviewers she was tired of keyboard voicings, so she picked up guitar with almost no experience and forced it into every track. Guests included 8485, Gabby Start and Maxwell Young, and the water tower on the cover was shot in Longport, New Jersey, the seaside setting behind the concept.

The Atlantic put it on its best albums of 2021, and The Line of Best Fit later named it among the greatest hyperpop albums. A DeadAir Legacy Edition with 24 tracks came out in February 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: 100 gecs · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician) · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.h: Opening for 100 gecs on the 10,000 gecs tour
years.p: The North American run started October 8 at the Fox Theater in Oakland and ended December 9 at Terminal 5 in New York.
years.xp: Lido put her in touch with manager Dorothy Caccavale, and Glaive and Blink-182's [[Travis Barker|3aebd566-7ff8-4b29-b017-051b6ec55861]] were already paying attention. The FADER quotes her saying that after Fishmonger took off she felt on autopilot and kind of vacant on this tour.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boneyard AKA Fearmonger · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician)
years.h: Boneyard AKA Fearmonger: Travis Barker on drums
years.p: The six-month writing block after Fishmonger ends with a companion EP, self-released, with Barker drumming on "Tongue in Cheek" and Brakence co-producing.
years.xp: The Atlantic's Spencer Kornhaber called it an improvement over Fishmonger, and The FADER called "Tongue in Cheek" a one-of-a-kind mosh pit. She has said she wouldn't open Ableton until she had a song idea, after five months of writing nothing.

years.p: Her first headline mini-tour ran February and March. By July she was playing the festival's opening day.

eras.title: Welcome to Wallsocket, Michigan
eras.text: She wrote a whole fictional town, ran an alternate reality game to sell it, and told NME hyperpop was dead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Wallsocket · Wikipedia: Underscores (musician) · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.h: Wallsocket: three girls, one Michigan town, no hyperpop
years.p: A concept album on Mom + Pop and Corporate Rockmusic, country and folk and emo, with gun violence, class and religion in the plot.
years.xp:
The rollout came with fake Wallsocket websites and an alternate reality game, modeled on the Halo 2 and Cloverfield campaigns she loved. Singles ran from "Cops and Robbers" on May 3 to "Old Money Bitch" on August 16, with Gabby Start on "Locals (Girls Like Us)".

Per Wikipedia, she called hyperpop officially dead in an NME interview that year. The FADER quotes her tying the album's numb, angry sound to antidepressants: "the anger and depression of not being able to feel anything." The Atlantic placed it seventh on its year-end list. A Director's Cut with four extra songs followed June 28, 2024.

eras.title: Music for malls
eras.text: Touring with Porter Robinson and Danny Brown, she wrote her most direct record in hotel rooms. Then Charli XCX took her on the road.

years.h: Coachella: she plays "Music" before anyone has heard it
years.p: The song came out June 27. She made the instrumental on the Porter Robinson tour and recorded vocals in Chicago with a mic that fit in a backpack.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she played both Coachella weekends and also aired "Copycats" with Danny Brown. The track is a loose homage to Madonna's song of the same name and a return to the dubstep and future bass she grew up on.

Pitchfork's Kieran Press-Reynolds called it endearingly askew, littered with little tonal jumps and ornate glitches. Mastering was by Heba Kadry.

years.h: "Do It": Dance Dance Revolution in the video, Britpop synths on the record
years.p: She directed the video herself. A remix with South Korean singer Yves premiered January 22, 2026.

years.src: Wikipedia: U (Underscores album) · The FADER: 9 takeaways
years.p: Pitchfork's Walden Green gave it 8.6 and praised the production detail. It has an 89 on Metacritic, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
She wrote it on the road and calls it music for malls, airports, hotels and supermarkets, drafting lyrics outside high-end stores and recording voice memos on escalators. She produced, mixed and mastered everything but "Music". The Guardian's Alexis Petridis found it less hair-raising than before, closer to late-90s and early-2000s R&B. The Sydney Morning Herald called it the first pop masterpiece of the post-Brat age.

She told The FADER it is the least poser-y she has felt.

years.h: The cover is a mall she walked to after school
years.p: Japanese illustrator Ochiai Shohei drew San Francisco's Stonestown Galleria. She did the design direction, he says, and he was on-site director.
years.xp: Each of her albums is tied to a real place: a New Jersey water tower, a Michigan horseshoe statue, now a mall she visited in high school. Ochiai first turned her down over scheduling, then messaged her on Instagram to say he wanted in. The art has yellow headphones near the middle and workers at a sandwich counter.

years.src: The FADER: 9 takeaways · underscores cover story
yt: FADER interview: opening for Charli xcx, personas, K-pop
years.h: FADER cover story: from the underground to the edge of the mainstream
years.p: Her word for what could be her ceiling, from the FADER's July cover story.
years.xp: She told the magazine she doesn't know what her ceiling is, "but it definitely feels like this could be it." The same story covers her K-pop idol dream, the 2ndgenbias YouTube channel, and umru describing her as once the quietest, most reserved person.

years.src: Charli XCX announces · Charli XCX Performs Live Debuts
years.h: She cancels her own fall tour to open for Charli XCX
years.p: Charli's Music, Fashion, Film Tour announcement said she gave up her headline dates to join every show.
years.xp: On July 10 she joined Charli at Music Hall of Williamsburg, a 650-capacity pop-up in Brooklyn, to sing "Music" as a duet. Clairo and Kim Petras also came out.

years.cap: Music, Fashion, Film Tour opener, Philadelphia
yt: Music, Fashion, Film Tour with underscores, Philadelphia
years.h: Tour opener in Philadelphia: Charli brings her out for "Do It"
years.p: At Xfinity Mobile Arena, Charli invited her back for a song from U.
years.xp: Stereogum reported the night also had the live debut of Charli's "Persona" and her first "Stay Away" in four years.
